segment_reference_payload.description: Segment's Google Cloud Pub/Sub destination publishes each event as a JSON message to a configured Pub/Sub topic. The topic name is taken from the Segment destination settings. Message attributes can optionally be derived from event fields for subscriber-side filtering. Segment sends the full event JSON as the Pub/Sub message data.
segment_reference_payload.integration_method: Google Cloud Pub/Sub Publish API via Google Cloud Client SDK

authentication.method: Google Cloud Service Account JSON credentials

config_fields.projectId: Google Cloud project ID containing the Pub/Sub topic
config_fields.credentials: Service account JSON key for authentication
config_fields.topicName: Pub/Sub topic name where events are published

pubsub_publish.message_format: Full event JSON serialized as message data bytes
pubsub_publish.attributes: Segment supports mapping event fields to Pub/Sub message attributes for subscriber filtering
pubsub_publish.ordering_key: Not typically set by Segment — messages are unordered by default

rudderstack_expected_payload.description: RudderStack's Google Pub/Sub producer receives JSON data with three top-level fields via the Produce method: 'message' (the event payload object), 'topicId' (string identifying which Pub/Sub topic to publish to), and optional 'attributes' (a map of string key-value pairs for Pub/Sub message attributes). The producer marshals the 'message' object to JSON bytes for the pubsub.Message.Data field, copies 'attributes' to pubsub.Message.Attributes, then publishes to the topic looked up from the pre-built topicMap (constructed during NewProducer from the eventToTopicMap destination config). Topics are mapped via the eventToTopicMap config array where each entry has a 'to' key specifying the target topic name.

connection.protocol: gRPC to Google Cloud Pub/Sub API

authentication.method: Google Cloud Service Account JSON credentials or Application Default Credentials

config_fields.credentials: Service account JSON key for authentication (passed via option.WithCredentialsJSON). Skipped if googleutil.ShouldSkipCredentialsInit returns true (for environments with Application Default Credentials).
config_fields.projectId: Google Cloud project ID — required; NewProducer returns error if empty
config_fields.testConfig.endpoint: Optional custom endpoint for testing (uses WithoutAuthentication and insecure gRPC when set)

publish_settings.CountThreshold: Configurable via Router.GOOGLEPUBSUB.Client.CountThreshold or Router.GOOGLEPUBSUB.noOfWorkers or Router.noOfWorkers (default: 64)

retry_config.retryCondition: Only retries on specific OAuth2 authentication credential errors; all other errors are permanent

produce_input_format.description: The Produce method receives json.RawMessage containing three fields: 'message' (event object), 'topicId' (string), and optional 'attributes' (map of string key-value pairs). The 'message' object is marshaled to JSON for pubsub.Message.Data. The 'topicId' is used to look up the pre-built Publisher from the topicMap. Attributes are copied to pubsub.Message.Attributes.

schema.message: <event payload object — marshaled to JSON bytes for pubsub.Message.Data>
schema.topicId: <string — maps to a topic in the eventToTopicMap, e.g., 'rudder-events'>

no_attributes.description: When the incoming payload has no 'attributes' field, the pubsub.Message is created with Data only and no Attributes map. This is the minimal valid publish path.

missing_message.message: [GooglePubSub] error :: message from payload not found

invalid_topic_id_type.message: [GooglePubSub] error :: Could not parse topic id to string

topic_not_in_project.message: [GooglePubSub] error :: Topic not found in project

publish_failure.description: gRPC status codes are mapped to HTTP status codes via getError(). The publish error message is prefixed with '[GooglePubSub] error :: Failed to publish:'

context_deadline_exceeded.message_pattern: [GooglePubSub] error :: Failed to publish:<deadline exceeded error>

invalid_project_id.description: Returned during NewProducer when projectId is empty

invalid_credentials.description: Returned during NewProducer when credentials JSON is malformed

topic_configuration.segment: Topic name is configured in Segment destination settings as a single topic per destination. Segment publishes all events from a source to the configured topic.
topic_configuration.rudderstack: Topic names are configured via the 'eventToTopicMap' array in destination config. Each entry has a 'to' key specifying the topic name. During NewProducer, a pubsub.Publisher is created for each topic in the map and stored in topicMap. The Produce method receives the target topicId in the payload JSON and looks it up in topicMap. This enables routing different events to different topics within a single destination config.
topic_configuration.parity_gap: RudderStack supports multi-topic routing per destination via eventToTopicMap, while Segment typically uses a single topic per destination. The topic name is resolved at different stages: Segment resolves at config time, RudderStack resolves at publish time from the payload's topicId field.

message_data.segment: Full event JSON is sent as the Pub/Sub message data bytes. The event includes standard Segment fields: type, event, userId, anonymousId, timestamp, properties/traits, context (with library.name=analytics.js), messageId.
message_data.rudderstack: The 'message' object from the Produce input is marshaled to JSON bytes via jsonrs.Marshal and set as pubsub.Message.Data. The event includes standard RudderStack fields plus additional envelope fields: rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt. The context.library.name identifies the RudderStack SDK.
message_data.parity_gap: RudderStack adds rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt to every event payload. The context.library.name field differs (rudder-sdk-js vs analytics.js). Pub/Sub subscribers processing events from both platforms must tolerate these additional fields.

message_attributes.segment: Segment supports configuring Pub/Sub message attributes derived from event fields for subscriber-side filtering. Attribute mapping is defined in destination settings.
message_attributes.rudderstack: RudderStack passes attributes directly from the 'attributes' map in the Produce input JSON to pubsub.Message.Attributes. Attribute values are extracted as string values from the gjson Map result. If no attributes are present in the payload, the message is published without attributes.
message_attributes.parity_gap: Both platforms support Pub/Sub message attributes, but the mapping mechanism differs. Segment configures attribute mapping in destination settings (declarative), while RudderStack expects attributes to be pre-computed and included in the Produce input payload (imperative). The Transformer service is responsible for computing attributes before they reach the stream manager.

ordering_key.segment: Segment does not typically set ordering keys on Pub/Sub messages. Messages are unordered by default.
ordering_key.rudderstack: RudderStack does not set pubsub.Message.OrderingKey. Messages are published without ordering guarantees at the Pub/Sub level. Event ordering is managed at the Router level via per-destination ordering guarantees before events reach the stream manager.
ordering_key.parity_gap: Neither platform sets Pub/Sub-level ordering keys by default. Both rely on application-level ordering before publish. No parity gap for ordering semantics.

authentication.segment: Google Cloud Service Account JSON credentials configured in destination settings
authentication.rudderstack: Google Cloud Service Account JSON credentials configured in destination config ('credentials' field). Validated via googleutil.CompatibleGoogleCredentialsJSON. Supports Application Default Credentials when googleutil.ShouldSkipCredentialsInit returns true. Supports custom test endpoints with insecure credentials for integration testing.
authentication.parity_gap: Both platforms use Service Account JSON credentials. RudderStack additionally supports Application Default Credentials and test endpoints — these are additive capabilities with no negative parity impact.

event_envelope_fields.segment: Standard Segment event fields: type, event, userId, anonymousId, timestamp, properties/traits, context (with library.name=analytics.js), messageId
event_envelope_fields.rudderstack: Standard RudderStack event fields: type, event, userId, anonymousId, timestamp, properties/traits, context (with library.name=rudder-sdk-js), messageId, plus rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt
event_envelope_fields.parity_gap: RudderStack adds rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt to every event payload. The context.library.name identifies the SDK origin. Subscribers must tolerate these additional fields.

error_handling.segment: Segment retries failed publishes based on its standard retry policy. Errors are surfaced in the Segment debugger.
error_handling.rudderstack: gRPC status codes from Pub/Sub API are mapped to HTTP status codes (see error_responses.publish_failure.grpc_code_mapping). Retry for authentication errors is configurable via Router.GOOGLEPUBSUB.Client.EnableRetries (default: false). When enabled, uses exponential backoff with configurable intervals. Non-authentication errors are treated as permanent failures.
error_handling.parity_gap: Different retry strategies: Segment uses its platform-level retry policy, while RudderStack has configurable per-producer retry with selective retry only for OAuth2 authentication errors. RudderStack provides more granular gRPC-to-HTTP error code mapping.

flow_control.segment: Flow control behavior is managed by Segment's internal pipeline infrastructure.
flow_control.rudderstack: Explicit flow control via pubsub.FlowControlSettings: FlowControlBlock behavior (blocks when limits exceeded), configurable MaxOutstandingMessages (default: 1000), configurable MaxOutstandingBytes (default: -1 unlimited). Additionally, NumGoroutines (default: 25), DelayThreshold (default: 10ms), CountThreshold (default: 64), and ByteThreshold (default: 10MB) control publisher batching.
flow_control.parity_gap: RudderStack exposes fine-grained flow control and batching configuration not available in Segment's Pub/Sub destination. This is an additive capability.

fields.credentials: Google Cloud Service Account JSON key string
fields.projectId: Google Cloud project ID — required (NewProducer returns error if empty)
fields.eventToTopicMap: Array of maps with 'to' key specifying topic names. A pubsub.Publisher is created per topic entry.
fields.testConfig.endpoint: Optional custom endpoint for testing environments

PubsubClient.pbs: pubsub.Client — underlying Google Cloud Pub/Sub client
PubsubClient.topicMap: map[string]*pubsub.Publisher — pre-built publisher map keyed by topic name from eventToTopicMap
PubsubClient.opts: common.Opts — shared options including Timeout duration

GooglePubSubProducer.enableRetry: Reloadable[bool] — toggle for retry on auth errors
GooglePubSubProducer.retryMaxRetries: Reloadable[int] — maximum number of retry attempts

produce_method_flow: 2. Validate client is not nil (400 if nil)
3. Create context with timeout from common.Opts.Timeout
4. Extract 'message' field from parsed JSON (400 if missing)
5. Marshal 'message' value to JSON bytes via jsonrs.Marshal (400 if marshal fails)
6. Extract 'topicId' string (400 if missing, non-string, or empty)
7. Look up Publisher from topicMap by topicId (400 if not found)
9. Build pubsub.Message with Data and optional Attributes
10. Publish via topic.Publish(ctx, message).Get(ctx) — with optional retry for auth errors
11. Map gRPC errors to HTTP status codes via getError() (504 for DeadlineExceeded/context timeout)
12. Return (200, 'Success', 'Message publish with serverID<id>') on success

critical_gaps.segment_behavior: Single topic per destination configured in settings
critical_gaps.rudderstack_behavior: Multi-topic routing via eventToTopicMap array; topicId specified per event in Produce payload
critical_gaps.impact: RudderStack supports more flexible topic routing — a superset of Segment's model. A single-topic configuration can be achieved by using a single entry in eventToTopicMap.
critical_gaps.mitigation: Configure eventToTopicMap with a single entry to match Segment's single-topic behavior

critical_gaps.segment_behavior: Declarative attribute mapping configured in destination settings — event fields are mapped to Pub/Sub attributes at config time
critical_gaps.rudderstack_behavior: Attributes are pre-computed by the Transformer service and passed in the Produce input payload as a map. The stream manager copies them directly to pubsub.Message.Attributes without applying its own mapping logic.
critical_gaps.impact: The attribute mapping logic lives in different layers: Segment applies it in the destination connector, RudderStack applies it in the Transformer before the event reaches the stream manager. Functionally equivalent if the Transformer is configured to produce the same attributes.
critical_gaps.mitigation: Ensure RudderStack Transformer destination transform produces equivalent attribute mappings to Segment's destination settings

non_critical_differences.description: RudderStack adds rudderId, originalTimestamp, sentAt, receivedAt to event payloads in the message data
non_critical_differences.impact: Pub/Sub subscribers must tolerate additional fields when processing events from RudderStack
Subscribers that branch on library name must handle both identifiers

non_critical_differences.description: RudderStack exposes fine-grained publisher settings (NumGoroutines, DelayThreshold, CountThreshold, ByteThreshold, FlowControlSettings) not available in Segment's Pub/Sub destination
non_critical_differences.impact: Additive capability — no negative parity impact; enables performance tuning for high-throughput scenarios

non_critical_differences.description: RudderStack has configurable retry logic specifically for OAuth2 authentication credential errors with exponential backoff
non_critical_differences.impact: Additive reliability feature — no negative parity impact; helps with transient authentication issues

non_critical_differences.description: RudderStack supports a testConfig.endpoint for integration testing with local Pub/Sub emulators using insecure credentials
non_critical_differences.impact: Development and testing convenience — no production parity impact

parity_summary.functional_equivalence: Both platforms publish JSON event data to Google Cloud Pub/Sub topics using the same Publish API. The core message data (event JSON) and attributes are functionally equivalent. The primary architectural difference is the topic routing model (single vs multi-topic) and the attribute mapping layer (destination connector vs Transformer). RudderStack's implementation is a superset of Segment's capabilities, with additional flow control, retry, and multi-topic features.

notes: Google Pub/Sub shared stream destination. Segment slug: google-cloud-pubsub. RudderStack package: services/streammanager/googlepubsub/. Both platforms use the Google Cloud Pub/Sub Publish API to deliver JSON event data. RudderStack's producer receives topicId, message, and optional attributes via json.RawMessage in the Produce method, then publishes via pre-built topic Publishers created during NewProducer from the eventToTopicMap config. Key differences: (1) RudderStack supports multi-topic routing via eventToTopicMap while Segment uses single-topic per destination, (2) attribute mapping is handled by the Transformer service in RudderStack vs the destination connector in Segment, (3) RudderStack adds rudderId/originalTimestamp/sentAt/receivedAt envelope fields, (4) RudderStack provides configurable flow control settings and authentication retry logic. Overall parity is high — Pub/Sub subscribers receive functionally equivalent event data from both platforms.
